T: Ten grand. One bad afternoon at the beach.
D: A young Kings Cross doorman loses a gangster's money at Bondi and has a day to get it back.
P: Serve the snacks when Jimmy heads down to Bondi.
S: the beach where the money goes missing
Flathead dusted in flour, dipped in a batter of flour and ice-cold lager, fried at 180C for 4 minutes, with thick chips, lemon and tartare, wrapped in paper and eaten on the sand.
Small beef pies braised 2.5 hours in stock and Worcestershire, baked in shortcrust with a puff lid, served sitting in mushy peas with tomato sauce on top.
the gangster's crew killing time at his place
Salted peanuts, pretzels and potato chips in bowls on the coffee table, with an onion dip of slow-cooked onions folded into sour cream.
M: a night out in the city
Squid scored and cut, dusted in rice flour and Sichuan salt and pepper, fried at 190C for 60 seconds, tossed with chilli and spring onion, with egg fried rice.
the family house out in the suburbs
Lamb leg studded with garlic and rosemary, roasted at 180C to 58C, rested, with roast potatoes and pumpkin, peas and gravy from the tin.
W: an Aussie dessert for a Sydney summer
Egg whites whisked with caster sugar until glossy, cornflour and vinegar folded in, baked at 120C for 90 minutes and cooled in the oven, topped with cream and passionfruit.
K: a cold one at a Sydney pub
Australian lager poured into chilled schooner glasses, a pint for anyone game.

s.note: the beach where the money goes missing
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry at 140C until soft. Whisk flour with ice-cold lager to a thin batter. Dip 600g flathead in flour, then batter, and fry at 180C for 4 minutes. Fry the chips again until crisp and wrap it all in paper with lemon and tartare.

Braise 800g diced beef chuck in stock for 2.5 hours, thicken and cool. Bake in shortcrust cases with puff lids at 200C for 30 minutes. Cook 500g peas and mash roughly with butter. Spoon peas into bowls, sit a pie on top and finish with tomato sauce.

m.note: a night out in the city
m.how: Score 500g squid tubes and cut into pieces. Toss in rice flour with ground Sichuan pepper and salt and fry at 190C for 60 seconds. Toss with chilli and sliced spring onion. Fry cold cooked jasmine rice with scrambled egg and spring onion and serve together.

w.note: an Aussie dessert for a Sydney summer
w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in a teaspoon each of cornflour and white vinegar. Shape into a round, bake at 120C for 90 minutes and cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream and passionfruit.

d.note: a cold one at a Sydney pub
d.how: Chill the schooner glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Pour the lager slowly down the side of the tilted glass, straightening up at the end for a neat head. Keep the rest in the fridge and pour a pint for anyone who is game.
